Troubleshooting and limitations¶

Installation and command errors¶

uv cannot find the pinned Python

Update uv using the installation method you originally used, then retry uv sync --extra dev --locked. If your platform has no compatible interpreter or dependency wheel, inspect that package’s error rather than silently changing numerical dependencies. Python 3.14.10 is the tested pin; an arbitrary later minor version is not necessarily supported by every wheel.

ModuleNotFoundError or poly-mpm: command not found

From the checkout root, run uv sync --extra dev --locked and use uv run --locked python MPM.py ball. For a pip environment, activate it first. python -m pip may be absent from a uv-created environment; use uv sync to manage that environment.

The example cannot be imported

Use its module name, such as ball, rather than inputs/ball.py. Put new modules under inputs/ and expose Params(args). Run the documented commands from the checkout root.

An example reports a usage error

Run uv run --locked python MPM.py --help to list examples, or uv run --locked python MPM.py <example> --help for its argument order, types, and choices. Missing, invalid, and extra arguments are rejected before setup. The Python loader raises ValueError for these errors. Check the example matrix for runnable commands.

For the square drum, use uv run --locked python MPM.py bi_square_drum 11 2. The arguments are the number of grid nodes per side (at least 3) and the finite, positive Froude number. For bi_dam_break, the arrangement must be top, bot, or mix. Grain size class counts must be at least two. silo accepts only its grid node count: use silo 11; its two size classes are fixed, and the formerly documented trailing 2 was ignored.

Unsupported material law

Check the exact registry name and Constitutive models. The retired elastic_time, ken_kamrin, and ken_simple implementations are not available. viscous_size and the separate legacy P.F compressible-fluid path are unimplemented. Four inputs remain deliberately unsupported: tunnel, poly_avalanche, tri_seg_test, and fluid.

Output and runtime¶

No plot window appears

Expected: figures are saved as PNGs. Check P.save_dir, the output flags, and whether the input replaces a default callback. output=False disables all output, including custom histories.

No files after a short preview

The preview may end before savetime, and an input’s custom callback may save only at save times. Set P.savetime=P.dt for a few steps and choose a separate directory, as in Getting started.

A run appears to take forever

Check dt, t_f, and plot frequency in the input. Some examples request millions of steps. Start with run(..., max_steps=100, output=False). The CLI has no generic duration or maximum-step switch. Ctrl-C interrupts a run but does not create a restart checkpoint or guarantee end callbacks run.

A Matplotlib cache warning appears

Matplotlib needs a writable cache/config directory. If your home directory is read-only, set MPLCONFIGDIR to a writable directory before starting Python; for example on macOS/Linux, MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/poly-mpm-mpl uv run --locked python MPM.py ball.

Numerical errors¶

A particle leaves the domain

The solver fails before invalid cell lookup. Check domain extents, inlet/ outlet or periodic configuration, velocity and loading, then timestep. Moving beyond an unconstrained grid edge is not an implicit free-surface boundary extension or an automatically expanding computational domain.

A model reports nonfinite state

The error identifies the law, material, timestep, field, and particle rows. Check parameter units, initial conditions, model domain, and timestep. Reduce the timestep as a diagnostic, then perform convergence checks. Finite output alone is not proof of an accurate or physically valid solution.

Grain fractions do not sum to one

Initial rows must be nonnegative and sum to one. Use phi of shape (ns,) or (n, ns). The segregation tests conserve species mass without clipping or renormalisation. Investigate inventory and boundary fluxes rather than enabling normalise_phi to hide drift.

What the solver currently does¶

This is a research solver with a regular 2D grid and explicit mechanics sharing one nodal momentum field. Updated mode evolves deformation/volume/density and supports linear/quadratic interpolation plus FLIP/PIC/APIC transfers. APIC requires a quadratic basis and planar motion. There is no GIMP, independent multi-body contact, general curved boundary, implicit/quasistatic solve, or checkpoint/restart. Rate-form plasticity is not a multiplicative finite-strain plasticity model. Legacy mode preserves the earlier numerical conventions explicitly.

See Numerical methods, Particle arrays and examples, Constitutive models, and Segregation transport for exact scope. Smoke-tested examples, equation checks, conservation tests, experimental validation, and convergence studies are different levels of evidence. Choose the evidence required for your application.

poly-mpm

2D material point method with grain-size segregation
